title: Seven Cards, Small Hand
statement:
Cards numbered $1, 2, \dots, 7$ are shuffled so that all $7!$ orderings are equally likely, and are then drawn one at a time in that order. Each drawn card goes into the player's hand. After each draw, the following rule is applied for as long as possible: if the hand contains the smallest-numbered card that has not yet been played, that card is played, which removes it from the hand. The player loses if, after this rule has been applied following some draw, the hand holds $3$ cards.

The probability that the player does not lose is $\frac{m}{n}$, where $m$ and $n$ are coprime positive integers. Find $m + n$.
hints: Look at where card $1$ sits in the ordering. No card can be played until card $1$ has been drawn, so what happens to the hand if card $1$ arrives late?

Card $1$ must be among the first three cards drawn. Set up a recursion on the number of cards: delete card $1$ from the ordering and compare the original game with the game played on the remaining cards.

Let $S(k)$ be the number of orderings of $k$ cards on which the player does not lose. If card $1$ is among the first three cards, deleting it leaves an ordering that is safe exactly when the original was safe, since from the draw of card $1$ onwards the two games have the same hand. This gives $S(k) = 3 \cdot S(k - 1)$ for $k \ge 4$, and $S(3) = 3!$ because a hand of three cards cannot occur with only three cards.
solution:
Let $S(k)$ be the number of orderings of $k$ cards with which the player never holds $3$ cards. Only relative order matters. The hand grows by at most one card per draw, so the player loses exactly when the hand at some point holds at least $3$ cards.

For $k=3$ the hand holds at most $2$ cards before the third draw. After the third draw every card has been drawn and played, so $S(3)=6$.

Let $k\ge 4$ and let card $1$ be in position $p$. If $p\ge 4$, nothing is played in the first three draws, so the hand holds $3$ cards and the player loses. Hence $p\le 3$.

Let $p\le 3$ and compare with the game on the same ordering with card $1$ deleted. Before card $1$ is drawn, the original hand has at most $2$ cards, and the reduced game has drawn at most $p-1\le 2$ cards, so neither game is lost during these draws.

For $t\ge p$, let $D$ be the first $t$ cards drawn, which contains card $1$. After the rule is applied, the played cards are the longest initial run $1,2,\dots,j$ contained in $D$, and the hand is the rest of $D$. The reduced game after $t-1$ draws has drawn $D\setminus\{1\}$, and its played cards are $2,\dots,j$, so its hand is the same set. Thus the original game is lost at draw $t$ exactly when the reduced game is lost at draw $t-1$. Hence an ordering with $p\le 3$ is safe exactly when its reduced ordering is safe.

Such orderings correspond bijectively to a choice of $p\in\{1,2,3\}$ and an ordering of the other $k-1$ cards. So $S(k)=3S(k-1)$, giving $S(7)=3^4\cdot 6=486$.

The probability is
$$\dfrac{486}{5040}=\dfrac{27}{280},$$
which is in lowest terms since $27=3^3$ and $3\nmid 280$. So $m+n=307$.
